newsitem.title: USA: Brisk soybean sales in Indiana, Illinois - crushers.
newsitem.headline: Brisk soybean sales in Indiana, Illinois - crushers.

text.p: Soybean crushers said purchases of old crop soybeans were brisk in Illinois and Indiana early Tuesday and some basis bids were falling in response.
"Bean basis has been retreating here all morning," said one soybean crusher in Indiana.
"I guess there were some beans out there after all, even with the basis at only 20 over (Chicago Board of Trade) August futures)," the dealer said.
On Monday, basis bids from soybean crushers in the Illinois and Indiana markets ranged from 30 to 40 cents per bushel over CBOT August futures.

Another dealer in Illinois said that his crushing plant was not bidding for soybeans anymore because because he had purchased enough late Monday and early Tuesday to meet crushing needs through the first two weeks of August.
"We are officially out of the market," the crusher said. "I've been buying beans all morning and we have just been run over."
Dealers speculated that the brisk sales were triggered by a rally in CBOT futures on Monday and Tuesday.
"Some people think this might be the market's last gasp before harvest," a merchandiser said.
Other dealers said there were a number of reasons for active sales at this time of year.
"I think people also want to be cleaned out by September to be ready for new crop, and they've also got big fertilizer bills coming due," a merchandiser said.
At 1107 CDT, August soybean futures were 10-1/4 cents per bushel higher at $7.68 a bushel and other months were up 12-1/4 to 18-1/4.
